intro: San Diego rewards visitors with beaches, a historic harbour and easy day trips to Mexico. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: MTS Trolley (light rail) links downtown, Old Town, Mission Valley and San Ysidro.
MTS buses cover the city; the #992 Flyer runs between SAN terminals and Santa Fe Depot.
Taxis are metered; Uber and Lyft operate widely and are usually cheaper.
A car is the most efficient way to see the sprawling county; expect rush-hour congestion.
Downtown and the bayfront are walkable; bikes and scooters are common near beaches.
The Coaster commuter train and Amtrak Pacific Surfliner serve the coast north to Oceanside and Los Angeles.

zoo.name: San Diego Zoo
zoo.price_text: Check current ticket price on the official site; one-day passes are often around USD 70–80 for adults
zoo.hours: Daily, usually 09:00–17:00 or later in summer; check on the day
zoo.tip: Go early and take the guided bus tour first to get your bearings, then walk the rest.

coronado.name: Coronado Beach
coronado.hours: Open all day; lifeguards usually daytime in summer
coronado.tip: Walk south toward the Hotel del Coronado for the classic view, and bring layers — it can be cool even in summer.

seaworld.name: SeaWorld San Diego
seaworld.price_text: Check current ticket prices online; buying ahead is usually cheaper
seaworld.hours: Usually daily, hours vary by season; check on the day
seaworld.tip: Book online in advance and arrive at opening to hit the big rides before queues build.

harbor_cruise.name: San Diego Harbor Cruise
harbor_cruise.price_text: Check operator prices; short cruises often around USD 30–40
harbor_cruise.hours: Departures through the day; check schedule on the day
harbor_cruise.tip: Take an afternoon or sunset departure for the best light on the skyline and the USS Midway.

belmont.name: Belmont Park
belmont.price_text: Free to enter; rides and the Giant Dipper cost extra
belmont.hours: Usually daily, hours vary; check on the day
belmont.tip: Ride the historic Giant Dipper wooden coaster and walk the boardwalk at sunset.

comiccon.name: San Diego Comic-Con
comiccon.price_text: Badge prices vary by day; badges sell out fast and are hard to get
comiccon.hours: Usually a long weekend in July; check the official dates
comiccon.tip: Badges are limited — plan months ahead, and enjoy the free downtown events even without one.

sesame.name: Sesame Place San Diego
sesame.price_text: Check current ticket prices online; advance tickets usually cheaper
sesame.hours: Seasonal; usually daily in summer, check on the day
sesame.tip: Best for families with young kids — bring swim gear for the water play areas.

ucsd.name: University of California, San Diego (UCSD)
ucsd.hours: Campus grounds generally open daily; buildings vary
ucsd.tip: See the Stuart Collection public art, including the giant 'Sun God' statue, on a campus walk.

jackbox.name: Jack in the Box
jackbox.price_text: Budget fast food; most items under USD 10
jackbox.hours: Many locations open long hours or 24h; check on the day
jackbox.tip: A San Diego-born fast-food chain — try the tacos, a local menu staple.

mundo.name: Mundo Divertido
mundo.price_text: Check current prices on site; family amusement park
mundo.hours: Hours vary by season; check on the day
mundo.tip: A family-friendly amusement park near the border — confirm opening days before you go.

qdoba.name: Qdoba
qdoba.price_text: Budget fast-casual; most meals under USD 15
qdoba.hours: Varies by location; check on the day
qdoba.tip: Quick fast-casual burritos and bowls — handy for a fast meal between sights.

gaslamp.name: Gaslamp Quarter walk
gaslamp.hours: Always open; liveliest in the evening
gaslamp.tip: Stroll the Victorian-era streets by day, then come back for dinner and nightlife.

lajolla_cove.name: La Jolla Cove
lajolla_cove.tip: Watch sea lions and seals from the cliffs — keep a respectful distance and don't approach them.

liberty_station.name: Liberty Public Market
liberty_station.price_text: Free to enter; pay per vendor
liberty_station.hours: Usually daily; check on the day
liberty_station.tip: A food hall in a former naval training building — good for a casual lunch with varied choices.

cabrillo.name: Cabrillo National Monument
cabrillo.price_text: Small entrance fee per vehicle or person; check current rates
cabrillo.hours: Usually daily daytime; check on the day
cabrillo.tip: Go for the tide pools and the sweeping view over the harbor and city skyline.

balboa.name: Balboa Park
balboa.price_text: Free to walk; museums charge separately
balboa.hours: Park always open; museums daytime, check on the day
balboa.tip: Walk the El Prado and the gardens, then pick one museum rather than trying to see them all.

sunset_cliffs.name: Sunset Cliffs
sunset_cliffs.tip: Come for sunset over the Pacific — stay back from the cliff edges.

old_town.name: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park
old_town.price_text: Free to walk; some sites charge
old_town.hours: Grounds usually open daily; check on the day
old_town.tip: A good stop for early California history and Mexican food nearby.

midway.name: USS Midway Museum
midway.price_text: Check current admission prices on the official site
midway.hours: Usually daily; check on the day
midway.tip: Allow a few hours — the self-guided audio tour on the aircraft carrier is the highlight.

stays.why: Walk to the bayfront, Petco Park and the Gaslamp restaurants. Trolley and #992 airport bus start here.
Quiet bayfront hotels, minutes from SAN airport and downtown. Good for early flights and families.
Walk to the cove, sea lions and snorkel spots. Upscale and calm; 20–30 minutes from downtown by car.
Cheaper chain hotels near the trolley and shopping. Central for driving to the Zoo and beaches.

food: Try a fish taco: grilled or fried fish, cabbage slaw and crema. Cheap stands and sit-down spots both do it well.
California burrito: carne asada, fries, cheese and salsa wrapped in a tortilla. A full meal for one.
Little Italy on India Street for pasta, pizza and a lively evening scene; book ahead on weekends.
Seafood by the water in Point Loma and the Embarcadero; check the day's catch and prices on the board.
Craft beer is big here. Many tasting rooms in North Park and Miramar; expect about $8–10 a pint.
more_time: Swap a beach afternoon for a day trip north on the Coaster or Pacific Surfliner to Oceanside or Encinitas.
Add a morning at Torrey Pines State Reserve: short cliff trails and ocean views; parking fills early, check on the day.
Cross to Coronado by ferry for the beach, the Hotel del Coronado and a slow lunch.
